results.title: Re-verify the #14 fixes on a full applied frame
results.requirement: The contrast, type-size and spacing fixes, verified on a complete applied frame rather than on the compiler output alone.
results.knownIssue:
PASS on 16 Oct 2026. Earlier in the session this was carried as an open failure because the hosted `create_design` timed out mid-transaction and committed a partial frame. It was latency, not an operation cap: the same 52-operation program later committed 32 operations before the client gave up, and re-issuing the compiler's own remaining operations in two smaller transactions completed the frame. A 17-operation and a 5-operation transaction both returned `success` with no timeout.

The frame is 57 nodes across three transactions, all from `compile_ir` output with only the parent references rewritten from transaction-local ids to the real Figma ids the previous transaction returned — the documented way to build across several calls, not a hand-written substitute.

Measured on the complete frame (node 317:414, applied at x=18000 on page Branding):

    nav label       #A8ABA0 on the #111111 rail   8.09:1   (was 3.82:1)
    device memory   11px                                 (was 10px)
    pill padding    4px top and bottom                  (was 2px)

review_design on all 57 nodes returns one finding, off-grid-geometry (minor). The four rules #14 touched — text-contrast, tiny-technical-text, off-scale-spacing and text-outside-autolayout — all report zero, where the pre-fix frame reported text-contrast and tiny-technical-text as serious and text-outside-autolayout 20 times.

The render also surfaced three defects the reviewer did not, recorded as L05, L06 and L07. This case closes; those three stay open.
results.detail: Complete 57-node frame applied and reviewed. Nav label 8.09:1 on the rail (was 3.82:1), device memory 11px (was 10px), pill padding 4px (was 2px). Review returns 1 minor finding; all four rules #14 touched report zero.

results.title: The active nav item's label takes the same fill as its own pill
results.requirement: A navItem with state 'active' paints its pill in the accent fill and must paint its label in a colour that reads against that fill.
results.knownIssue:
PASS on 16 Oct 2026.

The `navItem` emitter carried `#F2C94C` twice: once for the active pill and once for the active label. Rendering nodes 317:420 and 317:421 in isolation confirmed both resolve to the accent yellow, so the active item's label was invisible at 1.0:1.

First recorded as 'the label takes the rail's colour', which pointed at the #14 `onDarkSurface()` fix. That was wrong: the label never consulted the rail for an active item. The two colours were the same literal typed at two call sites, which is why they could drift — the same reason `hugSize` became a single source of truth. Both now read from `NAV_ACTIVE_FILL` / `NAV_ACTIVE_LABEL`.

`#111111` on `#F2C94C` measures 11.9:1. It is deliberately not derived from the rail, because the pill's fill is the same on every rail.

The review half of this mattered more. `text-contrast` returned zero findings on a 57-node frame containing a 1.0:1 pair: `effectiveSurface` only looked at the text's siblings, and a label sitting on its own painted parent has none, so it fell through to compositing the ancestors — measuring against the rail behind the pill. It now checks the parent's own fill, and no longer returns early when the client cannot supply a composited background.
results.detail: Active nav label is #111111 on the #F2C94C pill at 11.9:1 (was #F2C94C on #F2C94C at 1.0:1). review_design reports the same colour pair as a critical text-contrast finding.

results.title: A region covering a sibling goes unreported
results.requirement: Two sibling regions that share pixels must be reported, unless one is a backdrop painted before the other.
results.knownIssue:
PASS on 16 Oct 2026.

The rendered frame showed all three device nodes inside the dark nav rail, and the applied geometry put Topology at x=0 with width 1120 under a 220px rail at x=0.

Recorded first as a compiler bug in how `fill` measures from the left edge. That was wrong, and the correction is the substance of the case: compiling the full program offline puts Topology at x=252 with width 868 and the inspector at x=1120, which is correct. The overlapping geometry was produced by the L04 verification harness, which recompiled the tail operations from a reduced IR with the `nav` region missing — so `fill` had no left sibling to clear and resolved to x=0. The defect was in the evidence, not in the product.

The review rule was still added, because a harness that silently miscompiles is exactly the class nothing could see. `overflow` structurally cannot help: it asks whether a node leaves its parent, and a region inside its parent by definition does not.

`sibling-region-overlap` reports siblings sharing pixels, and decides the one legitimate case — a full-bleed backdrop painted first — by paint order rather than by geometry. The first version made that call from only one side of the pair, so the same backdrop passed or failed depending on which node the rule visited first.
results.detail: The compiler lays the stress program out with no overlapping regions (Topology x=252 w=868, Inspector x=1120). review_design reports the overlapping frame that was actually applied, and stays silent on backdrops, nested cards and edge-sharing panels.

raw.realCause: L04 harness recompiled tail ops from a reduced IR with no `nav` region

results.title: A connector between adjacent nodes is swallowed by its own arrowheads
results.requirement: A connector whose route is shorter than its arrowheads must not draw them, or the line disappears inside the heads.
results.knownIssue:
PASS on 16 Oct 2026.

link-0 emitted a createVector 10x10 whose path was a bare arrowhead outline, and it rendered as a small grey triangle in empty canvas belonging to nothing.

Recorded first as 'the connector has no endpoints and no span'. That was wrong on both counts. It had endpoints, and it had a route — a real one, between the two nodes the author named. What went wrong is that a cluster stacks its nodes 8px apart, so the chord between the two box edges is 8px, and each arrowhead is 8px. The heads covered the line completely and the vector normalised to the bounding box of the heads.

`routeConnector` now measures the chord and only draws heads when there is line for them to sit on. Below that it emits a plain line and says so in the layer name, so 'why is this a bare line?' is answerable from the file rather than from whoever happened to be looking at it.

`connector-endpoint-ambiguous` correctly stayed quiet throughout — there was a route, so there were endpoints, and they were on the nodes. The silence was the rule being right about a route that should not have been drawn that way.
results.detail: A connector between adjacent nodes emits a single-subpath line spanning the gap, with no arrowhead, and names the reason in the layer name. A connector with room keeps its arrowheads.

raw.before: createVector 10x10, path was an arrowhead outline only
raw.after: createVector 1x8, single subpath, layer name states the nodes are 8px apart

results.title: The product guard can no longer report PASS over unevaluated checks
results.requirement: A guard verdict must not read as approval while any of its own checks were left to a human judgement, and the guard must run on every build rather than only when asked.
results.knownIssue:
PASS on 17 Oct 2026, after the first attempt failed.

Before: `exo.primary-action-dominant`, `exo.selected-unambiguous`, `exo.technical-typography`, `exo.model-fit-context` and `exo.developer-apis` had no machine-checkable evidence. A rule in that state emitted `verdict: "PASS"` and counted itself in `stats.passed`, so a real program returned top-level PASS on the strength of eight structural checks while none of the five encoding design judgement had been evaluated. The count sat in `stats.manual`, underneath a verdict that read as approval.

After: a rule with nothing checkable reports INDETERMINATE, and so does a partly-checkable rule with any manual tail. `manual` fell from 8 to 2; the two survivors are genuine judgement calls and now say so.

Measured on the deployed build, against the live plugin: a latency set in a proportional face returns WARNING with `machineDataInProportionalFace=1`, and the same value with `valueStyle: "technical"` returns clean. Two controls claiming primary returns WARNING with `dominantActions=2`. A byte quantity returns clean, because the rule names addresses, latencies, hashes and identifiers and nothing else.

The guard now runs inside `executeRuntime` on every build. Verified live: four metric cards return `applicable: false` with `exo.no-generic-saas: maxComponents=4` as a blocking `product` violation — a generic SaaS card row that used to compile without complaint. The corrected program, with two cards, real status tones and a labelled edge, returns `applicable: true` with no warnings.

The full gated loop then ran end to end on the deployed build — guard, build, apply, review, render — which is the first time every stage has been exercised in one pass. Frame 344:1372, 33 nodes. `review_design` returned two minor findings (`off-grid-geometry`, `off-scale-spacing`) and nothing else: no text-contrast, no sibling-region-overlap, no overflow. The render shows the active nav label legible on its pill, both device nodes clear of the rail, and the labelled edge "serves 312 tok/s" set in the mono face between them. Frame removed afterwards.
results.detail: Guard verdict is INDETERMINATE, never PASS, while checks are unevaluated. Three formerly-manual truths are measured. The guard runs on every build and a product contradiction stops the build.
